validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE and CLASSIFICATION confirmed. This is a real, GAIL-built and operated pipeline: The Hindu Business Line (2018-02-02, quoting a GAIL company statement) and Governance Now (2018-02-05, same news cycle but independently written) both report GAIL placing a Rs 440-crore order to lay 350 km from Vijaipur to Auraiya, part of a ~665 km Vijaipur-Phulpur spurline feeding the JHBDPL/'Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga' project; the earlier 315 km Auraiya-Phulpur contract was awarded November 2016. India Investment Grid (indiainvestmentgrid.gov.in, a Government of India investment-tracking site — institutionally independent of GAIL's own press office) lists the project as 'Vijaipur-Auraiya-Phulpur Pipeline Project and LMC', Central PSU promoter, total cost USD 251.48m, completion/COD 2022-03-26, traversing Guna/Ashoknagar/Shivpuri/Datia (Madhya Pradesh) and Jhansi/Jalaun/Auraiya (Uttar Pradesh). A Lok Sabha unstarred-question reply dated 2022-07-21 (mirrored at indiangovtscheme.com, a reproduction of the official PIB/parliamentary answer on 'One Nation One Gas Grid') lists 'Vijaipur-Auraiya-Phulpur spur line' (item 20) among 'fully operational Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipelines', states 'Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh' — this independently confirms both existence AND that PipelineType=transmission is correct (a common-carrier trunk line, not gathering/distribution/feeder classification) AND that Fuel=Gas is correct. offshore-technology.com (a commercial pipeline-intelligence database, a fourth, methodologically distinct origin) separately profiles the same asset: GAIL owner/operator, onshore gas pipeline, Madhya Pradesh to Uttar Pradesh, ~2022 operational date. Four independent origins (2 press outlets on one GAIL statement + 1 Indian-government investment tracker + 1 commercial database + the Lok Sabha reply as a 5th, government, origin) all agree this pipeline is real, GAIL-owned, common-carrier/transmission, and gas. DUPLICATE check against the full 35-row India-gas roster: not a duplicate of P0925 (Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur/HVJ), despite sharing the Vijaipur and Auraiya nodes — HVJ (commissioned 1987, 3,474 km, ends at Jagdishpur) has a compressor station at both Vijaipur and Auraiya per Wikipedia, but this pipeline is a genuinely separate, newer (2016-2022) parallel corridor that diverges at Auraiya toward Phulpur rather than continuing to Jagdishpur; it is explicitly described in sources as built 'to debottleneck the upstream network of the JHBDPL project' (GAIL CMD B.C. Tripathi interview, Indian Infrastructure, 2018-09-20), i.e. new pipe, not a relabel. Not a match to GREP-I/II (P3297/P3299, Vijaipur-Dadri) or DVPL-I/II (P0919/P3298, Dahej-Vijaipur) either — different destinations. No duplicate flag warranted.

validity.researcher_notes: StartState/Province is currently 'Gujarat' in the live sheet (verified directly against data/GGIT_gas.csv, row ProjectID=P0957) — this is WRONG. Vijaipur, the pipeline's start point, is in Guna district, Madhya Pradesh, not Gujarat. Confirmed independently and unambiguously by FOUR separate origins: (1) The Hindu Business Line, quoting GAIL's own company statement: 'laying 350-km pipeline from Vijaipur in Madhya Pradesh to Auraiya in Uttar Pradesh'; (2) Governance Now, same underlying news but an independently-written piece: '...from Vijaipur in Madhya Pradesh to Auraiya in Uttar Pradesh'; (3) India Investment Grid (Government of India site), which lists the districts traversed as Guna, Ashoknagar, Shivpuri, Datia — all in Madhya Pradesh — before Jhansi, Jalaun, Auraiya in Uttar Pradesh; (4) offshore-technology.com's independent commercial-database profile, which states the pipeline 'will start in Madhya Pradesh'. The Lok Sabha 2022-07-21 reply also lists the pipeline's states as 'Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh'. There is no source anywhere describing a Gujarat endpoint or routing for this pipeline — Gujarat appears to be a data-entry confusion with GAIL's other Vijaipur-anchored corridors that DO touch Gujarat (DVPL/Dahej-Vijaipur, P0919/P3298, whose OTHER endpoint Dahej is in Gujarat). EndLocation/EndState (Phulpur, Uttar Pradesh) is correct and does not need changing.

validity.researcher_notes: LENGTH: sheet = 667.00 km. GAIL's own 2018 company statement (via The Hindu Business Line and Governance Now, two independently-written pieces on the same underlying GAIL statement) puts the total spurline at 'around 665 km' (350 km Vijaipur-Auraiya order + 315 km Auraiya-Phulpur contract awarded 2016 = 665 km). offshore-technology.com and the GAIL CMD's own 2018 interview (Indian Infrastructure, indianinfrastructure.com) both independently give 672 km. GEM's 667 km sits within this 665-672 km band (a <1.1% spread, plausibly reflecting planned-vs-as-built or route-refinement differences across the project's multi-year phased construction 2016-2022); not treated as a material (>10%) conflict, so no concern flagged, but recorded as a caveat rather than a clean single-figure confirmation. CAPACITY: sheet = 3.2 bcm/y. The gem.wiki page's own citation for this figure is a 2016 'India Invest' PDF at indianembassy.org.sa, which I confirmed is now a dead link (ConnectionError on live fetch) — so that original source cannot be checked. The only other source I could find repeating 3.2 bcm/y is offshore-technology.com's commercial database profile; I could not independently confirm whether that figure was itself sourced from GAIL/GEM-adjacent material or derived separately, so I am not treating it as a confirmed independent second source (tier low on this value specifically). A GAIL CMD interview (Indian Infrastructure, 2018) that mentions this pipeline by name does NOT give any capacity/MMSCMD figure for it (a web-search summary snippet appeared to attribute a '16 MMSCMD' figure to this pipeline, but on reading the actual article text that figure is not present for this specific line — flagging that near-miss so it isn't mistakenly treated as a second source later). Net: 3.2 bcm/y is plausible and unopposed, but not corroborated to the >=2-independent bar; left as-is (not filled, not overwritten), Capacity [ref] below is staged at tier=low accordingly.

fills.researcher_notes: Lok Sabha unstarred-question reply (2022-07-21, mirrored at indiangovtscheme.com) explicitly lists 'Vijaipur-Auraiya-Phulpur spur line' among 'fully operational Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipelines'. offshore-technology.com's independent commercial database separately profiles it as operational since ~2022. Two independent origins agreeing on Status=operating.
Both the government Lok Sabha reply (listing it under 'Natural gas pipelines') and offshore-technology.com's independent database entry ('gas pipeline') confirm the fuel is natural gas.

The Lok Sabha reply classifies it as a 'Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipeline' (India's regulatory term for an open-access long-haul trunk line) and offshore-technology.com profiles it as a long-distance onshore gas pipeline feeding a national trunk system (JHBDPL). Neither source uses the literal word 'transmission', so tier=medium rather than high, but both independently support the transmission-trunk classification over gathering/distribution/feeder.

India Investment Grid (Government of India tracker) gives 'Project Completion Date: March 26, 2022' / 'Completion Certificate/COD'. The Lok Sabha reply dated 2022-07-21 independently lists the pipeline as already 'fully operational' by that date. Two independent government-adjacent origins both place commissioning in 2022, consistent with StartYear1=2022.

DATA-QUALITY NOTE, not just a ref gap: the live sheet currently has DelayType='confirmed' populated but Delayed itself BLANK (verified directly against data/GGIT_gas.csv) — an internally inconsistent pairing per the schema (DelayType should not be populated while Delayed is blank). Evidence points to Delayed='yes' being the correct value that was dropped: GAIL's own CMD, in a 2018-09-20 interview (Indian Infrastructure), described Phase 1 (Auraiya-Phulpur) as 'expected completion by December 2018'; independently, India Investment Grid (Government of India) records actual completion/COD as 2022-03-26 and the Lok Sabha reply confirms full operation only by July 2022. That is a >3-year slip past the originally stated target — solid (though not airtight/officially-labelled-'delay') evidence supporting Delayed='yes', which would also resolve the DelayType/Delayed inconsistency already in the sheet. Tier=medium because the delay is inferred from schedule slippage across sources rather than a source explicitly using the word 'delayed'. Route to Update to apply.

Only one usable source found for this value (offshore-technology.com, 'Capacity: 3.2 billion cubic meters per year'). The wiki page's own original citation for this figure (a 2016 'India Invest' PDF at indianembassy.org.sa) is a dead link (ConnectionError). This pipeline is a dedicated GAIL feeder line, not on PNGRB's common-carrier itemised register (it does not appear in the 2026-05-31 NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf by name, consistent with the orchestrator's guidance that dedicated/tie-in lines are folded into PNGRB's grand totals rather than itemised), so the usual PNGRB cross-check is not available here.
